clue.text: When topless man's announced?

indicators.note: a topless word has lost its head, so the first letter of each word it governs is dropped
something announced is spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a man in chess can be a knight; with its silent head gone it is said the same way

explanation.surface: A party where a stripper is introduced to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: WHEN loses its top to give HEN; the chess man KNIGHT, topless and spoken, gives NIGHT. The whole clue also describes the moment at a hen party when the stripper appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelorette party in Britain often features a male stripper, so the whole question describes the occasion.

clue.text: To suppress America, His Highness stifled rising

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the royal abbreviation wraps around the country

parts.note: HH is the abbreviation for His Highness

explanation.surface: A complaint that America's voice is being smothered by royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a scandal quiet is to suppress it; the phrasal verb means conceal from public knowledge.

clue.text: Light gas without energy floats around tank to begin with

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the physics symbol is taken out of the gas

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: to begin with points at the opening letter of each of the words just before it

parts.note: the heads of three consecutive words

explanation.surface: Gas without energy drifts around a tank, like a technical report on buoyancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Light food is low in calories, and a non-fat product such as yogurt is marketed in exactly that way.

clue.text: Preposterous to describe mum using colloquialisms

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw a line around it, so one word goes round the other

explanation.surface: Someone protests that it is absurd to talk about their mother in slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describe' in its geometric sense means to draw a line round something, as when a compass describes a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic speech is natural, everyday native phrasing, which is what talking in colloquialisms amounts to.

clue.text: Oh golly! Falling — not seriously — for society girl

indicators.note: something falling tumbles over and lands in disorder, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation as someone falls for a socialite, though not in earnest.
explanation.walkthrough: Holly Golightly is the heroine of Truman Capote's Breakfast at Tiffany's, played on film by Audrey Hepburn.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional Holly is a glamorous New York party girl living off wealthy admirers, a classic socialite figure.

clue.text: Revolutionary Judea inspires very familiar feeling

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the rearranged word takes a letter inside it
a revolution overturns the existing order, so the place name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A revolution in ancient Judea stirs up a strong sense of having been here before.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names the uncanny sense that a new experience has happened before, which is a familiar feeling.

clue.text: Some contents taken from refrigerator: famous inspiration for poetry

indicators.note: only part of what is inside the next word is taken out, so the letters lie within it

parts.note: sitting inside the word, after the first few letters

explanation.surface: Someone raids the fridge, and the snack inspires a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is one of the nine Muses, the one presiding over love and lyric verse.

clue.text: Draws a tableau originally with expanses of land

indicators.note: originally refers to the origin, the very start, of the word before it

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a scene of wide open countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' pretends to be about sketching; here it means pulls in.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to pull people in, the same sense as a magnet that pulls metal towards it.

clue.text: Buckle under in the morning temperature? Inconceivable

indicators.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape, so the word that follows is twisted into another order

parts.note: T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: Someone collapses under the morning heat, an outcome nobody could have imagined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never imagined even in a dream is beyond thought, hence unthinkable.

clue.text: Actress, one embraced by dissolute rake, chivalrous in conversation

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside another's arms, so the numeral goes within the other word
dissolute means loose-living and disorderly, so these letters are rearranged
words in conversation are heard rather than read, so we want the sound alone

parts.note: behaving like a knight, said aloud

explanation.surface: A film star is courted by a debauched rogue who nonetheless speaks gallantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes inside RAKE, and the whole is scrambled to give the first name.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the English star of Pride and Prejudice and Pirates of the Caribbean, a well-known film performer.

clue.text: Star, laid back, is old timer

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word laid from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written before turning round

explanation.surface: A relaxed celebrity is described as a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' reads as relaxed and 'old timer' as a veteran; both are wordplay tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow-casting dial is an ancient device for telling the hour, so it is a timekeeper from long ago.

clue.text: Staged tea dance without a pirouette

indicators.note: a pirouette spins round on the spot, so the remaining letters are turned into a new order
without a means one letter of that kind is removed from the phrase

explanation.surface: An afternoon dance is put on, minus the twirls.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea dance is a genteel afternoon dance with refreshments. One of its two As goes, leaving seven letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that is put on before an audience is performed, which is one meaning of acted out.

clue.text: Peacekeepers assembled with a marine to demilitarise

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers gather with a marine to strip a region of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove weapons from an army or area is to disarm it, and the rarer verb has the same meaning.

clue.text: Visiting university, Australian redhead drained one firkin at first, large amount of booze

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's place, so the following letters sit within the college name

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for Australian

indicators.note: a drained word has had its insides emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: just the outside pair of letters

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An Aussie redhead at college downs a whole cask of beer in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: A firkin is a small beer cask holding nine gallons. The college name opens after its first letter to take the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tall glass about three feet long holding over two pints of beer, traditionally downed in one as a drinking feat.

clue.text: Act oddly, shake rump, getting as low as you can

indicators.note: oddly means take the letters in odd-numbered positions of the word before it

explanation.surface: A dance instruction to behave strangely and wiggle your behind, getting right down low.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at the lowest possible point, the very bottom of a decline in prices or fortunes.

clue.text: Butterfly variety seen in books on Italy and Portugal

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one word sits within the abbreviation for scripture

parts.note: Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A type of butterfly is spotted in Italian and Portuguese guidebooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' looks like part of the butterfly definition; it supplies RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common European species of white butterfly whose males have bright coloured wingtips.

clue.text: Champions see soup's prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been chopped and mixed, so the words before are reworked

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Prize-winning cooks look on as their soup is made ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champions' reads as a noun for winners; here it is a verb meaning supports.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt and promote a cause is to back it publicly, the verb sense of championing it.

clue.text: Jazz outfit thumping lute with bone

indicators.note: thumping beats things about, knocking the following letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A jazz band beats a lute with a bone, a scene of rough percussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' suggests clothing or a band; here it means a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Note Records is the celebrated American jazz record label, a company being an outfit.

clue.text: Is circle flat? Possibly … doubtful

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the preceding letters

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a circle can be flat, met with scepticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who constantly questions their own work is full of self-doubt, a loose but fair sense of the definition.

clue.text: North-west town's sportsman (forward)

explanation.surface: A footballing hero from a Lancashire town is a striker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a football position but just means ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolton is a large former mill town near Manchester in North West England.

clue.text: Answermust include the ancient city

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one abbreviation surrounds the article

parts.note: a misprint for 'Answers must'; ans. is the standard abbreviation for answers

explanation.surface: A rule that a solution has to feature a historic city.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue runs two words together, a typo for 'Answers must'; the abbreviation opens after its first letter to hold the article.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital was a great city-state of classical antiquity, the home of Socrates and Plato.

clue.text: Everyman misrepresents height a fraction

parts.note: an ordinary person, anyone at all, as in 'one does'

indicators.note: to misrepresent is to present wrongly, so the next word is reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: The setter fibs about how tall they are, slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman is this puzzle's own pseudonym, and the everyman is the generic person, ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in eight is a number less than a whole, written as a numerator over a denominator.

clue.text: Write-in candidates including South American

indicators.note: the words before contain the letters within them, spanning the break between two words

explanation.surface: An election ballot with unofficial candidates, one of them from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire ruled much of the Andes in Peru before the Spanish conquest, so its people were South American.

clue.text: German army's spirit

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
an old word for a great army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: The fighting morale of German troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests morale in the surface; it means a phantom.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit is the soul of a dead person appearing to the living, a phantom or spectre.

clue.text: Patient's ill — nearly about to amputate limb, to begin with

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word wraps round the next word
nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
to begin with picks out the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A hospital patient is so sick that a limb is about to come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like the hospital noun; it is the adjective meaning enduring calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship without complaint, so the adjective describes calm, uncomplaining endurance.

clue.text: Withholding sex appeal, not a Beatles song primarily wanting for orchestration!

definitions.text: Withholding sex appeal, not a Beatles song primarily wanting for orchestration!

indicators.note: orchestration arranges music for performance, so the remaining letters are arranged anew
to withhold something is to keep it back inside, so the rearranged letters hold the short word
not a means one letter of that kind is struck out of the band's name
wanting means lacking, so the selected letter is also removed
primarily points at the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: an old slang word for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A Beatles track arranged without any sexy swagger.
explanation.walkthrough: Two letters go from the band's name before the rest is rearranged around the slang word. The whole clue then describes the song itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Let It Be is the title track of the band's final released album, a famous Beatles song.

clue.text: Grim-sounding novelist

indicators.note: sounding means we hear the word rather than see its spelling

explanation.surface: A writer with a gloomy reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century Irish-born author of Tristram Shandy, so he is a writer of fiction.

clue.text: They say Mr. Broadbent's tired with sportswear

indicators.note: they say signals what people say out loud, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: is tired: breathes hard, gasps; it sounds the same either way

explanation.surface: Gossip that a well-known actor is worn out from exercising in his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Jim Broadbent is the English actor of Iris and the Harry Potter films. Someone who pants is out of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers or shorts worn for exercise are athletic clothing, hence sportswear.
